title: Sprint Garden: Private instance prioritization grid and quarterly scenario matrix
creator: Priya Nair
description: Create a decision-ready prioritization grid (the 'Sprint Garden') for Private/VPC/on‑prem features to inform quarterly commitments, OKR mapping, and tranche releases. The goal is to produce a playbook and scenario matrix that the PM/ENG/DES guilds can use during sprint planning: 1) a four-quadrant prioritization grid (customer impact vs. operational cost), 2) three release scenarios (Aggressive / Balanced / Conservative) with capacity failure-budgets and rollback gates, and 3) an OKR mapping table linking features to org metrics (uptime SLA, activation time, cost/week). Deliverables: roadmap deck, prioritization spreadsheet, risk/mitigation appendix, and acceptance criteria for each release tranche.
acceptance_criteria: Quadrant grid published with scoring rubrics and sample scored features (>=20 features)
Three release scenarios documented with explicit capacity assumptions and failure budgets
OKR mapping ties each tranche to measurable signals (SLOs, activation time, unit cost)
Stakeholder signoff from ENG infra lead and Head of Sales for customer-risk thresholds
Playbook includes rollback criteria, canary gating, and customer communication templates
work_items: Collect feature backlog and assign scoring attributes (impact, engineering effort, compliance risk)
Run two prioritization workshops with Solutions and Sales to capture customer sensitivity bands
Model capacity runway for three release scenarios using historical Dedicated telemetry
Draft tranche-level acceptance tests and canary metrics for Console and Runtime teams
Publish roadmap deck to Confluence and circulate to leadership for review
decisions: Adopted four-quadrant scoring (customer impact / ops cost) instead of weighted RICE for clarity to GTM
Require a minimum of one performance regression test per tranche before canary release
Set conservative scenario as default for regulated customers unless contractual SLA buy-down approved
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Overcommitting in Aggressive scenario could violate failure budgets - Mitigation: limit Aggressive tranche to 2 non-critical features
Risk: Compliance gating adds unpredictable QA delays - Mitigation: add dedicated compliance buffer in Balanced scenario
Risk: Regional capacity constraints for on‑prem pilot customers - Mitigation: sequence pilots by region and reserve burst pool
